solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shop beginning to trade in live fish

definitions.note: a verb: to inform on someone

indicators.note: the first letter of trade is placed within the words for live and fish

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a ray is a flat sea fish

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word trade is all that is used

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper starting a sideline dealing in live fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' looks like a noun for a store, but here it is the slang verb meaning to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police, a kind of treachery.

clue.text: Session for one writer in retreat

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters for these words are read from the end

parts.note: e.g., short for exempli gratia, means for example or for one
a nib is the point of a pen, a writer by metonymy

explanation.surface: A writer heading off on a retreat for a solitary working session.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a spell or bout of indulgence, an extended session of eating or drinking.

clue.text: Malign exchange about University College

indicators.note: the word for exchange goes round the abbreviation, as about means surrounding

parts.note: to trade is to exchange goods
UC is the standard abbreviation for University College

explanation.surface: A spiteful exchange of words concerning a university college.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to speak ill of someone and damage their reputation unfairly.

clue.text: Where one may hear tenor interrupting Carmen by second half of aria

indicators.note: the tenor's letter breaks into the middle of the letters from Carmen

parts.note: read as car plus men: AUDI is a car make, OR (other ranks) are men in the army
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

indicators.note: only the back two letters of the word aria are used

explanation.surface: A tenor breaking into a performance of Carmen during the second half of an aria.
explanation.walkthrough: Carmen is not Bizet's opera: split it as car plus men, a German car make and the army's other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditoria are halls where an audience sits to listen, so they are places for hearing.

clue.text: Body or exterior of vehicle?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a case is an outer covering or shell

explanation.surface: A question asking whether body means the bodywork of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Car bodywork is a red herring; the body is a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcase, a variant spelling of carcass, is a dead body, especially an animal's.

clue.text: Protestant sect cut short Sabbath wrongly

indicators.note: the name of the sect loses its last letter, being docked at the end

parts.note: the Amish are a Protestant sect in America

explanation.surface: A Protestant sect wrongly cutting short its Sabbath observance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the final H off AMISH, leaving AMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: If something goes amiss it goes wrongly, the adverb meaning astray or awry.

clue.text: Pirate recording of rude song

indicators.note: a recording captures speech, so the words are taken by how they are spoken

parts.note: coarse means rude and an air is a song

explanation.surface: A bootleg copy of a rude song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pirate' looks like a verb for illegal copying; it is the noun, a sea robber.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a pirate, especially one raiding along the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Speed with which author gets point

parts.note: Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels
a ness is a headland or point of land

explanation.surface: How fast an author gets to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiftness is quickness of movement, the same quality as speed.

clue.text: Warning fencing's about to start blocking neighbouring gardens

indicators.note: a block of letters is cut from the middle of the doubled run, the outer letters falling away
the word gardens is set beside a second copy of itself, as neighbours are side by side

explanation.surface: A neighbour warning about a fence going up between adjoining gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neighbouring' writes gardens twice, GARDENSGARDENS; 'blocking' takes a block from across the join, a hidden word in effect: garden-S-garde-ns.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencers call this French phrase, meaning on guard, to warn that a bout is beginning.

clue.text: Resistance jamming broadcast to assist attack

indicators.note: jamming means forcing into, so the resistance letter is pushed inside the word for broadcast

parts.note: to air is to broadcast
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
to aid is to assist

explanation.surface: The wartime Resistance jamming enemy broadcasts to help an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An attack by aircraft dropping bombs on a target is called by this name.

clue.text: Constable's first to portray new male icon

definitions.note: read as constable is, the 's being a link

indicators.note: only the opening letter of portray is taken
made new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painting by Constable as the first to portray a new male icon.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable looks like the painter John Constable; it is a police officer. 'new' rearranges MALE ICON to OLICEMAN after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is the lowest rank of officer in a British police force.

clue.text: Take away those that are charged for valid reasons

parts.note: to deduct is to subtract or take away
ions are atoms or molecules carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Fees taken away for charges made on supposedly valid grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Deductions are conclusions reached by logical reasoning from premises, sound inferences.

clue.text: Booze repeatedly brought back sex appeal

indicators.note: two words for sex appeal are each turned around, the word repeatedly saying the phrase is used twice

parts.note: both IT and SA are crossword shorthands for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Drink keeps bringing back someone's sexual allure.
explanation.walkthrough: Sex appeal is used twice: SA reversed gives AS and IT reversed gives TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Physical stress is clear to the audience

indicators.note: as heard by listeners, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: sheer means clear or transparent, as in sheer fabric

explanation.surface: Physical stress made plain for listeners to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics shear is a stress acting parallel to a surface, deforming a material.

clue.text: Breakfast viewers reported issue in a number of episodes

definitions.text: issue in a number of episodes

indicators.note: reported speech is spoken, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: cereal is a breakfast food and eyes are what we view with

explanation.surface: Audiences of a breakfast TV show reported watching a drama issued in episodes.
explanation.walkthrough: Breakfast viewers looks like people watching morning TV; it is cereal plus eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: To serialise a story is to publish or broadcast it in instalments.

clue.text: Imprison leaders of encrypted terrorist communications infrastructure

parts.note: to intern is to confine or imprison, especially in wartime

indicators.note: the first letters of the following two words are taken

explanation.surface: Jail the ringleaders behind a terrorist cell's encrypted messaging network.
explanation.definitionFit: The global network of linked computers is the backbone that carries modern communications.

clue.text: Time to study English philosopher's routine

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: An English philosopher's daily routine of time set aside for study.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a tedious, repetitive routine one cannot escape, from the exercise machine.

clue.text: Put out and angry about instruction to reduce speed

indicators.note: the word for angry goes round the musical instruction

parts.note: irate means angry
rit., short for ritardando, is the musical direction to slow down

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed and angry at a sign telling drivers to slow down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put out is annoyed, so to put out a person is to annoy them.

clue.text: Cutting edge dental equipment

parts.note: sounds like the latest gadgetry in a dentist's surgery, but means a tooth with a sharp cutting edge, part of the mouth's own equipment

explanation.surface: An advert for the latest high-tech dentistry tools.
explanation.definitionFit: The front teeth are shaped with a sharp edge for cutting food, natural dental gear.

clue.text: Mitigates complaints not involving detective inspectors

indicators.note: the letters for the detective inspectors are left out of the word for complaints

parts.note: diseases are illnesses, medical complaints
DI is the police abbreviation for detective inspector, so two are DIS

explanation.surface: Someone smooths over grievances by keeping senior police out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaints' looks like grievances; it means illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain or trouble is to lessen it, just as mitigating makes something less severe.

clue.text: Tot's feet caught in twisted reins

definitions.note: read as tot is, the 's being a link

indicators.note: the abbreviation for feet is trapped inside the rearranged letters
twisted reins are tangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A toddler's feet tangled up in the reins of a harness.
explanation.walkthrough: Tot looks like a small child but is a small drink of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A snifter is a small measure of spirits, just as a tot is a small dram.

clue.text: Fine material found in continental crust

indicators.note: the answer is found lying within the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A fine mineral discovered in the Earth's continental crust.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into a very fine powder.

clue.text: GP wants extensive treatment for Joanna

wordplay.reading: G P written out in full

parts.note: the letters G and P ask to be expanded to the full words they abbreviate: G for grand and P for piano

explanation.surface: A family doctor insists on a long course of treatment for a patient called Joanna.
explanation.walkthrough: GP looks like a doctor; it is the two letters, each expanded. Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano, so Joanna looks like a patient's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Joanna rhymes with piano in Cockney rhyming slang, so it names the instrument.

clue.text: Figure out leaving university causes trouble

indicators.note: worked out, so the letters of figure are reordered

explanation.surface: Figuring out why someone leaving university causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FIGURE once its U goes, as 'leaving' says.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to grief or to give someone grief is to have or cause trouble and distress.

clue.text: Born desperately short of essentials?

parts.note: nee means born, used before a woman's maiden name

indicators.note: the word loses its essential middle, keeping just its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone born into dire poverty, lacking the basics of life.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: someone born badly lacking necessities is in want.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy people are poor, lacking the necessities of life.

clue.text: Waterproof material used to paint family

parts.note: oils are oil paints, used to paint pictures
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Waterproof fabric pressed into service for painting by the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilskin is cotton cloth treated with oil so that rain runs off it.

clue.text: Inventor yielding nothing ruined trader in hock?

indicators.note: wrecked, so the letters of inventor are thrown into a new order

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An inventor whose work earned nothing is ruined and in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yielding' means giving up the O, and 'ruined' rearranges what is left. In hock looks like in debt; hock is German white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintner deals in wine, and hock is a German white wine from the Rhine.

clue.text: Communist paper taking on artist to create new sketch

indicators.note: the paper takes on the artist, adding those letters ahead of its own

parts.note: red is a common term for a Communist
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
FT, the Financial Times, this very newspaper

explanation.surface: A Communist newspaper hiring an artist to produce a new cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraft is to write a fresh version of a draft or outline.

clue.text: Commotion when anger consumes both sides

indicators.note: the word for anger swallows up the letters for both sides
both says each of the two sides is treated in turn, so the left one goes into the word for anger separately from the right

parts.note: fury is great anger
the first of the two sides, L for left
the other of the two sides, R for right

explanation.surface: A commotion when rage takes over people on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumes' and 'both' say FURY takes in each side separately, L after the F and R after the U, rather than LR as one block.
explanation.definitionFit: A flurry is a sudden burst of activity or excitement, a commotion.
